summary: Writing to Laurence Housman from the Riviera at the end of December 1898, Wilde praised the Napoule fisher-folk as an ideal race with no morals and named two of them as his special friends: Raphael and Fortuné, 'both quite perfect, except that they can read and write'. That sentence is the whole of the record for him - no surname, no age, no occupation stated, no second mention anywhere in the correspondence read. The single-month span is the date of the evidence, not a claim about duration.

sources.quote: The people here – fisher-folk all – have beautiful eyes, crisp hair of a hyacinth colour, and no morals: an ideal race. I have two special friends, one called Raphael, the other Fortuné – both quite perfect, except that they can read and write.
sources.context: Wilde to Laurence Housman, [Circa 28 December 1898], Hôtel des Bains, Napoule - the third paragraph of a four-paragraph letter that opens on the pinewoods and thanks Housman for a drawing.
sources.supports: The whole of the record for Raphael: named as one of Wilde's two special friends among the Napoule fisher-folk, called quite perfect, with no outcome recorded
